discovery: Aberration-corrected electron optics enabling sub-angstrom transmission electron microscopy

nominees.name: Harald Rose
nominees.affiliation: Technische Universität Darmstadt / Ulm University, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics / electron optics
motivation: For half a century Scherzer's theorem held that round electron lenses have unavoidable spherical aberration, limiting electron microscopes far above atomic resolution. Harald Rose devised a hexapole corrector design that overcomes this limit. Maximilian Haider and Knut Urban turned it into a working instrument, and in 1998 they demonstrated the first aberration-corrected transmission electron microscope. This was a triumph of first-principles physics carried through by careful engineering. Correctors are now standard, and they let us image individual atoms, point defects, dislocation cores, interfaces and light elements such as oxygen and nitrogen with picometre precision. In my own field this changed the study of radiation damage in steels and nuclear fuels: defect clusters and precipitates that earlier we could only model are now measured directly. The same holds for semiconductors, catalysts, batteries and quantum materials. Few instrumental advances have changed so completely what experimentalists can see.
